purpose: adjudicate the epoch-7 pre-start performance headroom defect and the section-12.6 census-counter compliance gap, both inside the already authorized four-path surface

issued_by.impersonation_disclaimer: Not a human reviewer and not the owner.

part_0_reviewer_error_owned.statement: from the run-2 snapshots the reviewer proved that the 55.35 GiB drop in data-volume free space equalled the 53.96 GiB peak swap allocation, and then asserted that the ordinal-3 disposable child was the allocator and named the epoch-7 real-lineage census as the probable site. The arithmetic was sound; the attribution was not derivable from it. Standalone measurement refuted both claims: the child peaks at 1.17 GiB with zero swapouts, and the active ordinal-3 path does not reach _real_lineage_census before the first checkpoint at all.
part_0_reviewer_error_owned.rule_tightened: system-wide swap growth may establish that memory was demanded somewhere, never by which process; naming a suspect site requires a per-process resident-set measurement or a call-graph proof before it is put in writing to the operator

part_3_ruling.scope_ruling: both repairs proceed inside the existing authorized surface under the six-field epoch-7 authority at commit 06336a9f593ede4132be73a8c8a087df18db904b; no new owner authorization is required
part_3_ruling.scope_reasoning: epoch 7 has not landed and no candidate has been delivered, so this is pre-delivery iteration on the same four authorized M paths, exactly as epoch-5 r2 and r3 and epoch-6 r2 proceeded under their own surface authorities. The surface is unchanged, no capability is added, and no gate, threshold, sample, seed, model, prompt, contract, gold, schema, ledger or mirror byte is touched.

binding_constraints: the registered 180-second checkpoint limit must not be raised, relaxed, made configurable, or bypassed; raising it would mask the defect rather than remove it
no validation may be weakened: every fact proven today about the continuation mirror and the second-copy history must still be proven, with the same strictness and the same failure modes

follow the epoch-6 r2 precedent at implementation commit e5aab9772793a7b0465f100cb48f99a1bc4e45dc: bind names to seal-time commitment roots and stop reading payloads on the hot path, rather than caching or parallelising payload retention

output identity must be proven, not assumed: on identical inputs the repaired code must produce byte-identical started.json, candidate, terminal, evidence, control and history roots. The two premirror runs already pin started.json at ffd15b310c1b72ac3a317240db1b7a2dd64005015bc2ef251e86b785cb4f2d1a; the repaired build must reproduce that digest from the same premirror state.

the sealed ordinal-2 evidence is unaffected and must not be regenerated: it is bound to immutable epoch-6 Git blobs by the historical anchor, while the repaired bytes are covered by the epoch-7 live anchor
repair_1_prestart_performance.acceptance_threshold: the standalone premirror probe must show started.json produced within 60 seconds, giving at least a threefold margin against the 180-second limit, reported with maximum resident set size and swapouts delta from the same probe at digest afbced8ecc02d70ec61dcadb569c8a4d0f238e1131f00b7d17b581710be44ded. A margin measured in single-digit seconds is not acceptable at any host quietness.

gap_accepted_as_reported: real-lineage census Git operations are not incremented into deterministic counters
producer sealed counters initialize git_objects_read to zero
validator git_objects_read is a post-hoc raw-touch estimate rather than actual Git object or subprocess work
census completes before the current work-bound assertion, so it cannot fail fast
registered tests verify constants and direct over-limit dictionaries but not census work against the bound
repair_2_section_12_6_counters.reasoning: r1 section 12.6 is approved design that the reviewer passed. Landing epoch 7 with a work bound that cannot fail fast on the very path the design named would put a known non-compliant implementation on main and would leave the F-17 class undetected by the mechanism built to detect it. It is therefore closed in the same round, not deferred.
binding_constraints: counters must record actual Git object and subprocess work performed by the census, not an estimate reconstructed from results
the bound must be evaluated incrementally so that it fails fast during the census, not after it completes
the validator must recompute the counters independently and must never accept producer-reported values
registered tests must exercise real census work against the bound, in both modules, including a positive that stays under the bound and a negative that trips it mid-census
